answers.answer: Yes, as classified in SCOPe 2.08 they are placed in the same family. d1s9za_ ("Amyloidogenic design-1", sunid 98768, sccs k.40.1.1) and d1hqja_ ("Unnamed design-1", sunid 61142, sccs k.40.1.1) both fall under family k.40.1.1, "Designed trimeric coiled-coil" (sunid 100905). Their lineages diverge at the protein-entry level (sunids 103785 and 100906, both under the same parent 100905) and converge at the family node, so the 2.08 records do not support any claim that they belong to different families. Caveats: (1) For designed proteins, SCOPe family membership reflects a classification grouping of a shared designed coiled-coil architecture, not inherited common descent; these are de novo designs, so 'homologous' here means same SCOPe family assignment, and it should not be read as evolutionary ancestry. (2) The names "Amyloidogenic design-1" and "Unnamed design-1" are SCOPe protein-entry labels, not functional annotations, so they do not establish amyloidogenicity, function, or any transferable biological property. (3) Same-family placement is a database assignment and does not by itself establish sequence or structural identity between the two domains; confirming that would require a structure or sequence comparison of the two coordinate sets, which this API does not provide. (4) Answers here are for the base SCOPe 2.08 release; the 2.08-2026-08-16 periodic update was listed but not separately checked.
